comments.story_title: A philosophy-quoting homeless man in China has fled internet fame
comments.why_zh: 人们为何追求地位和名气
comments.quote_zh: 这部纪录片让人大开眼界
comments.text_zh: 这部纪录片让人大开眼界：[VIDEO]（虽然它超过 2 小时，我第一次看的时候睡着了）。但 TL;DW：人们总是在寻求地位，因为地位意味着别人认可并称赞他们。而当今的名人文化意味着出名似乎是获得地位的一条捷径。在一个更好的社区里，你会有朋友喜欢你、认可你，因为他们了解了你和你的品格。
comments.text: This doc is eye-opening: [VIDEO] (although it's over 2 hours and I fell asleep the first time I watched it). but TL;DW: People are always looking for status, because status means others acknowledge and praise them. And today's celebrity culture means being famous is seemingly a quick way to gain status. With a better community you'd have friends who like you and acknowledge you because they got to know you and your character.

comments.quote_zh: 这部（2个多小时）关于地位的纪录片相当发人深省
comments.text_zh: 奢侈品是身份象征，我们买它们是因为渴望地位，因为内心深处我们渴望社会里他人的认可。所以我想，是不是城市化/越来越孤独的趋势才是问题。如果你有一个紧密团结的社群，你会遇到因为你的品格、幽默感或和你相处愉快而欣赏你的人，而不是因为你开豪车。而如今我们其实不再有真正的社群了，只有互联网造成的两极分化，人们试图通过贬低别人来让自己感觉更好。这部（2个多小时）关于地位的纪录片相当发人深省：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Luxury goods are status symbols, we buy them because we crave status because deep down we crave recognition from others in society. So I wonder if urbanization/the trend towards more loneliness is the problem. If you have a tightly-knit community, you'd have people who appreciate you because of your character, sense of humor or good company; not because you drive a fancy car. And nowadays we don't really have real communities anymore, just polarization through the Internet, where people try to feel better about themselves by putting down others. This (2+ hours) documentary about status is quite eye opening: [VIDEO]

comments.why_zh: 关于地位和优绩主义的长纪录片
comments.quote_zh: 关于地位的有趣超长纪录片
comments.text_zh: 我浏览了一遍那篇书评，它似乎是在抨击这本书以及它试图提出的论点。但我好奇：如果别人把豪车看作地位，那我开着豪车出现，就意味着我带着地位出现。如果我是女性，拎着 Louis Vuitton 包出现，那也意味着带着地位出现，但拎 Michael Kors 包呢？就像几年前一位女性朋友跟我说的：“呃，大家都买那个牌子，它现在都‘廉价’了。”……关于地位的有趣超长纪录片：[VIDEO]，它也谈到“优绩主义”以及美国那种“只要努力就会成功”的观念，而这暗含了它的反面：“如果你穷，那说明你懒”。
comments.text: I skimmed through the review, it seems it's skewering this book and the arguments it's trying to make. But curious, if other people see expensive cars as status, me showing up in a fancy car means me showing up with status. If I'm female and I show up with a Louis Vuitton bag, that also means showing up with status, but with a Michael Kors bag? As a female friend told me a few years ago "Ewww, everyone buys that brand, it's now 'cheap'."... Interesting long-ass documentary about status: [VIDEO] , but also about the "meritocracy" and the US' idea of "If you work hard you'll be successful" which imply the flip of it: "If you're poor, that means you're lazy".

comments.author: netsharc
comments.why_zh: 部分讲述努力与运气的纪录片，从 28 分钟开始
comments.quote_zh: 这部两个多小时的纪录片部分谈到了这一点，尤其是从约 28 分钟开始
comments.text_zh: 太多人信了美国梦那一套：“只要你足够努力，你就会成功。”如果你相信这个，那你就得相信它的反面：“如果你又穷又不成功，那说明你不够努力，你肯定很懒。”还有太多靠信托基金的孩子，或者父母有钱、能送他们去昂贵学校（或有钱住在学校经费充足的学区）的孩子，会把运气撇到一边，并相信“我成功了，那一定说明我是个勤奋又聪明的打工人”。另外，要小心幸存者偏差：这里的大多数人都会有相似的路径（天生聪明、良好教育、高薪 IT 工作、巨大成功），大概也会对努力和运气持有相似的看法……这部两个多小时的纪录片部分谈到了这一点，尤其是从约 28 分钟开始：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Too many people buy the American dream of "If you just work hard enough, you'll be successful.". If you believe this, then you'd have to believe the opposite: "If you're poor and unsucessful, that means you didn't work hard enough, you must be lazy.". And too many trust-fund kids or kids from rich parents who could afford to send them to expensive schools (or rich enough to live in a district with a well-funded school) dismiss their luck and believe "I'm successful, that must mean I've been a diligent and smart worker.". Also, beware of survival bias, most of people in here will have similar paths (born with smarts, good education, high-paying IT job, great success) and probably have similar beliefs about hard work and luck... This 2+ hour documentary partly talks about it, in particular from ~28m: [VIDEO]

comments.text: Here's a 143 minute citation: [VIDEO] Or a 6 minute one: [LINK] TL; DW: the flip side of the American/Protestant work ethic which says "Work hard and you'll surely succeed" is that then you'd have to logically view that the people who are failing/have failed in life are lazy. On the topic of status, I can see why racists are threatened by a more equal society: it would mean the black family would be just well-off as them, and it would suck to not feel superior to "those lazy people". I guess this isn't much of a citation...

comments.author: netsharc
comments.story_title: Ask HN: Can you imagine a world where anybody could do any job?
comments.why_zh: 关于地位焦虑的长纪录片
comments.quote_zh: 看完这部关于地位焦虑的（长）纪录片之后[1]
comments.text_zh: 如果你有脑瘤，能直接叫邻居帮你把它切掉，那倒挺有意思——不过我想你多半还是得租一间手术室。我猜人类会像通用计算机，可以被编程去做任何事（假设所有计算机配置都一样）。你说的是“艺人”，所以我想知道，如果人们自己也能同样胜任表演或唱歌，他们还会不会对别人的表演感到惊叹。照这个设想，人类是不是得变成 Borg 个体那样？但回到劳动力市场，我猜没人会因为自己是“少数几个”能给某个外卖服务的 webapp 设计 JSON 的人而拿到六位数薪水——这种事谁都能做！人们还是会买食物，因为也许不是每个人都想当农民；人们也还是会买机票，因为没有足够资源给每个人都造一架飞机（或一间手术室）。看完这部关于地位焦虑的（长）纪录片[1]（或更短的总结：[2]）后，我喜欢从这个角度看事情。如果我们都擅长管理财富，劳动力市场还会有财务顾问吗？如果我们人人平等，我们还会追逐财富吗（在我看来，我们追逐财富主要是因为它是地位象征）？[1] [VIDEO] [2] [LINK]
comments.text: It'd be interesting if you had a brain tumor and could just ask your neighbor to operate it out - but I guess you'd still need to rent an operating room. I guess humans would be like general purpose computers that you can program to do anything (let's assume all of the computers are equally specced). You said "entertainer", so it makes me wonder if people will still be wowed by acting or singing performances if they could also do it as competently. Would humans have to be like Borg units in this scenario? But to return to the labor market, I guess no one get's paid 6 figures because they're "one of the few" that can architect the JSON for a webapp for some food delivery service, everyone can do that! People would still buy food because maybe not everyone wants to be a farmer, and people would still buy plane tickets because there are not enough resources to build everyone a plane (or an operating room). After watching this (long) documentary about status anxiety[1] (or shorter summary: [2]) I like to see things from that perspective. Would the labor market have financial advisors if we're all competent at managing our wealth, would we even be chasing wealth (which we mostly do because IMO it's a status symbol) if we're all equal? [1] [VIDEO] [2] [LINK]
